name: Vector
description: GeoJSON vector layer (points/lines/polygons, annotations, arrows, gradients) with time, injectable params, dynamic-extent geodatasets, filtering and per-feature attachments.

supportedData.label: GeoJSON
supportedData.description: A GeoJSON FeatureCollection of points, lines and/or polygons. The primary vector input; supports per-feature style properties, {starttime}/{endtime} time filtering and injectable URL variables.
supportedData.procurement: Export from any GIS (QGIS, ogr2ogr -f GeoJSON) or author by hand.

supportedData.label: KML
supportedData.description: Keyhole Markup Language vector features, converted to GeoJSON on load.
supportedData.procurement: Export from Google Earth or ogr2ogr -f KML.

supportedData.label: GeoDataset (PostGIS-backed vectors)
supportedData.description: A vector dataset uploaded via 'Manage Geodatasets' and served from PostGIS through the internal API. Enables dynamic-extent (viewport) requerying for large datasets.
supportedData.procurement: Upload a GeoJSON in Configure → Manage Geodatasets.

supportedData.label: STAC feature source
supportedData.description: Features derived from a STAC API, catalog, collection or item, loaded as GeoJSON.

supportedData.label: Runtime API features
supportedData.description: GeoJSON fetched from an arbitrary API endpoint (with injectable time/variable params) rather than a static file.

components.name: Layer Name
components.description: A display name for the layer.

components.name: Initial Visibility
components.description: Whether the layer is on initially.

components.name: Source Type
components.description: What the 'Source URL' is meant to reference. See the 'Source URL' description for more.

components.name: Source URL
components.description:
• URL: '{url}' - A file path that points to a geojson or .kml file. If the path is relative, it will be relative to the mission's directory.
• GeoDatasets: '{geodataset_name}' - Simply go to 'Manage Geodatasets' at the bottom left, upload a geojson and link to it in this URL field with '{geodataset_name}'
• API: 'publishedall' - Grabs all features published via the DrawTool.
• API: 'published:{file_intent}' - Grabs all features published via the DrawTool of a certain intent. Possible values are: roi, campaign, campsite, signpost, trail, all
• API: 'drawn:{file_id}' - Grabs a user drawn file from the DrawTool. The file_id is an integer and can be found by hovering over the desired file in the DrawTool. Note that if the file chosen is still private, the file owner will be the only user who can view it.
• STAC: '{url_to_stac}' - Point to a STAC catalog/collection/item of GeoJSON features.
• STAC-CATALOG: '{url_to_stac_catalog}' - Use this prefix if the URL is specifically to a Catalog object.
• STAC-COLLECTION: '{url_to_stac_collection}' - Use this prefix if the URL is specifically to a Collection object.
• STAC-ITEM: '{url_to_stac_item}' - Use this prefix if the URL is to an Item object
• If the underlying data is a COG or similar data product, use the Tile layer type instead.

components.name: Minimum Zoom
components.description: The lowest (smallest number) zoom level for which to show this layer. If the current Map's zoom level is less than this, the layer will not be rendered even if the layer is still on.

components.name: Maximum Zoom
components.description: The highest (greatest number) zoom level for which to show this layer. If the current Map's zoom level is higher/deeper than this, the layer will not be rendered even if the layer is still on.

components.name: 3D Layer Type
components.description: Whether, in the Globe, to clamp this layer onto the ground textures or to represent with sprites and line objects.

components.name: Initial Opacity
components.description: A value from 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque) of the layer's initial opacity.

components.name: Controlled
components.description: Whether the layer can be dynamically updated via the JavaScript API or not. If true, the layer can be dynamically updated and the URL is not required. If true and a URL is set and Time Enabled is true, the initial url query will be performed.

components.name: Color
components.description: The border color of each feature. If the feature is a line, this field is the color of the line.

components.name: Color From Property
components.description: Color but taken from each individual feature's property. For example 'color' or 'path.to.prop.in.properties.object'. Takes priority over the value in the 'Color' field.

components.name: Opacity
components.description: Stroke Opacity

components.name: Opacity From Property
components.description: Opacity but taken from each individual feature's property. For example 'opacity' or 'path.to.prop.in.properties.object'. Takes priority over the value in the 'Opacity' field.

components.name: Fill Color
components.description: Fill Color

components.name: Fill Color From Property
components.description: Fill Color but taken from each individual feature's property. For example 'fill_color' or 'path.to.prop.in.properties.object'. Takes priority over the value in the 'Fill Color' field.

components.name: Fill Opacity
components.description: Fill Opacity

components.name: Fill Opacity From Property
components.description: Fill Opacity but taken from each individual feature's property. For example 'fill_opacity' or 'path.to.prop.in.properties.object'. Takes priority over the value in the 'Fill Opacity' field.

components.name: Weight
components.description: Stroke weight in pixels of point features.

components.name: Weight From Property
components.description: Weight but taken from each individual feature's property. For example 'weight' or 'path.to.prop.in.properties.object'. Takes priority over the value in the 'Weight' field.

components.name: Radius
components.description: Radius in pixels of point features.

components.name: Radius From Property
components.description: Radius but taken from each individual feature's property. For example 'radius' or 'path.to.prop.in.properties.object'. Takes priority over the value in the 'Radius' field.

components.name: Shape
components.description: A marker symbol for point features for this layer. When set to 'None', a simple circle is used. Marker icons and other attachments may override this setting.

components.name: Shape From Icon
components.description: Shape but taken from the Material Design Icon (mdi) library. Takes priority over the value in the 'shape' field. See https://pictogrammers.com/library/mdi/

components.name: Shape From Property
components.description: Shape but taken from each individual feature's property. For example 'shape' or 'path.to.prop.in.properties.object'. Takes priority over the value in the 'shape' and 'shape from icon' fields. Shape values are formatted like the dropdown options but all lowercase. Material Design Icon (mdi) icon names are also supported values.

components.name: Shape Rotation Offset
components.description: A original offset by which the rotate the original shape/icon so that it is natively pointing up. Useful with Attachment - Marker Bearings where, for instance, a plane with a bearing is desired but the plane icon natively points leftward.

components.name: Animation
components.description: Animation effect for vector features. All animations are synchronized across the map for visual consistency. Options include opacity effects, CSS filters, and subtle transforms.

rows.subdescription: Styles each feature from one of its properties - colour by depth, widen by confidence - instead of giving every feature the same look. Rules are applied over the styles above, and a feature's own 'style' property still wins over both. The Legend Tool displays whatever scale these rules describe; it does not assign anything.

components.name: Enable Dynamic Style
components.description: Turns the rules below on. Off, the layer is styled by the fields above alone.

components.name: Is User Settable
components.description: Lets a viewer re-aim the style from the Layers Tool - a different property, ramp, domain or bins - for their session only. Off, the layer is coloured as configured and there are no controls to change it.

components.name: Dynamic Style Rules
components.description: Each rule maps one property to one style attribute. A rule missing what it needs is ignored rather than breaking the layer.

object.name: Property Type
object.description: Whether the value styling a feature is the feature's own property, or a statistic of the geodataset group it belongs to - so a feature can be coloured by how its group compares rather than by itself. Group statistics need a 'Group Id' and are requested automatically.

object.name: Property
object.description: The feature property whose value decides the style, e.g. 'depth' or 'meta.reading.value'. For a Stats rule it is the numeric field to summarize per group instead. A viewer may only re-aim the layer at a property that has a rule, so what is listed here is what they can choose between. The options are the layer's own properties; a nested path can be typed.

object.name: Stat
object.description: Which of the group's statistics to style by. A viewer may switch between them without the rule being rewritten.

object.name: Defaults
object.description: How a value becomes a look. These are what a viewer starts with, and what they may change for their own session when 'Is User Settable' is on.

object.name: Styles
object.description: The style attribute this rule sets. Each rule sets one, so colouring by depth and widening by confidence are two rules.

object.name: Color Ramp
object.description: The colormap a numeric rule colours with, for the 'fillColor' and 'color' attributes. Defaults to viridis.

object.name: Reverse Ramp
object.description: Runs the color ramp from high to low.

object.name: Discrete
object.description: Divides the domain into flat bins instead of a smooth gradient.

object.name: Bins
object.description: How many bins a discrete rule divides its domain into. Defaults to 5.

object.name: Style Min
object.description: For the numeric attributes (fillOpacity, opacity, weight, radius): the value the low end of the domain maps to.

object.name: Style Max
object.description: For the numeric attributes: the value the high end of the domain maps to.

object.name: Scale
object.description: The span of data the styles above are stretched over.

object.name: Domain
object.description: Where the low and high ends of the scale come from. 'auto' uses a geodataset's dataset-wide statistics when it has them and the loaded features otherwise. 'fieldStats' is the whole dataset, 'loaded' only what has been fetched, 'stddev' is the average plus or minus a few standard deviations (so one wild outlier doesn't flatten the ramp), and 'literal' is the Domain Min and Max below.

object.name: Sigma
object.description: How many standard deviations the scale spans either side of the average. Defaults to 2 - which keeps one wild outlier from flattening the ramp for everything else.

object.name: Data Min
object.description: The low end of the scale. Set either end to pin it and let the other be discovered.

object.name: Data Max
object.description: The high end of the scale.

object.name: No Data
object.description: What a feature looks like when the rule has nothing to say about it.

object.name: No Data Value
object.description: The style value for a feature whose property is missing or isn't a number. Left empty, such a feature keeps the layer's ordinary style.

object.name: Unmatched Value
object.description: The style value for a categorical feature whose value matches no mapping. Left empty, it keeps the layer's ordinary style.

object.name: Values Are
object.description: 'numeric' stretches a ramp or a range over the property's numbers. 'categorical' matches its values against the mappings below.

object.name: Categorical Mappings
object.description: What each value of the property looks like.

object.name: Categorical Mappings
object.description: For a categorical rule: what each value of the property looks like.

object.name: Property Value
object.description: The value to match, compared as text.

object.name: Label
object.description: How the legend labels this value. Defaults to the value itself.

object.name: Color
object.description: The colour for this value, when the rule styles a colour attribute.

object.name: Number
object.description: The value for this mapping, when the rule styles a numeric attribute.

rows.subdescription: Uses an icon image instead of an svg for all of the layer's point markers. If you're using this as a bearing marker, make sure the base icon is pointing north.

components.name: Icon URL
components.description: A URL to an image to use as a marker icon.

components.name: Shadow URL
components.description: An optional URL to an image to use as a marker icon's shadow..

components.name: Icon X Size
components.description: Pixel width of the icon's image.

components.name: Icon Y Size
components.description: Pixel height of the icon's image.

components.name: Shadow X Size
components.description: Pixel width of the icon's shadow.

components.name: Shadow Y Size
components.description: Pixel height of the icon's shadow.

components.name: Icon X Anchor
components.description: X point of the icon which will correspond to marker's center location.

components.name: Icon Y Anchor
components.description: Y point of the icon which will correspond to marker's center location.

components.name: Shadow X Anchor
components.description: X point of the shadow which will correspond to marker's center location.

components.name: Shadow Y Anchor
components.description: Y point of the shadow which will correspond to marker's center location.

components.name: Time Enabled
components.description: True if the layer is time enabled. URLs that contain {starttime} or {endtime} will be dynamically replaced by their set values when the layer is fetched. If true and a URL is set and Controlled is true, only the initial url query will be performed.

components.name: Time Type
components.description: How time filtering is performed: • local - Downloads the entire file first, then filters features client-side based on their time properties (e.g., a timestamp field in the GeoJSON). If a refresh interval is set, the file will be re-downloaded periodically and then filtered locally. • requery - Re-requests the URL with {starttime} and {endtime} injected as parameters, expecting the server to do the time filtering. Does not filter client-side.

components.name: Time Format
components.description: The string format to be used in the URL for {starttime} and {endtime}. Uses D3 time format specifiers: https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format. Default: %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ

components.name: Start Time Property Name
components.description: Optional and only in use if Time Enabled = true and Time Type = Local. The starting time property path. For geodatasets with time columns already set, leave this field empty. Leave this field empty  Setting this is addition to Main Time Property Name casts the feature's time over a range instead of as a single point in time. Can use dot-notation for nested path. Can be a unix timestamp or an ISO time (end the ISO with a Z to designate that it should be treated as a UTC time).

components.name: Main/End Time Property Name
components.description: Required in Time Enabled = true and Time Type = Local. The main time property path. For geodatasets with time columns already set, leave this field empty. Can use dot-notation for nested path. Can be a unix timestamp or an ISO time (end the ISO with a Z to designate that it should be treated as a UTC time).

components.name: Refresh Interval Enabled
components.description: If 'Time Enabled' and 'Refresh Interval Enabled', this layer will automatically refresh/requery its data every 'Refresh Every N Seconds'. This is useful when the layer's data updates at some uniform cadence. Be aware that this may be an expensive operation depending on the amount of data a layer needs and the number of layers that have this enabled.

components.name: Refresh Every N Seconds
components.description: If 'Time Enabled' and 'Refresh Interval Enabled', this layer will automatically refresh/requery its data every n seconds. If null or 0, defaults to 60.

components.name: Data Start Time
components.description: The earliest time for which data is available in this layer. This is for display purposes only and does not constrain queries. Format: ISO 8601 datetime string (e.g., 2020-01-01T00:00:00Z).

components.name: Data End Time
components.description: The latest time for which data is available in this layer. This is for display purposes only and does not constrain queries. Format: ISO 8601 datetime string (e.g., 2025-12-31T23:59:59Z).

components.name: Legend From URL
components.description: A URL to a static image or .csv with the following header: 'color,strokecolor,shape,value'. If the path is relative, it will be relative to the mission's directory. This legend is overridden if a legend is also configured below.

components.name: Legend Orientation
components.description: Displays the legend horizontally or vertically.

components.name: Hide layer name
components.description: Hide layer name in the legend.

components.name: Convert to Dynamic Style
components.description: Legend entries no longer style features. This turns any entry with 'Style Matching' on into the equivalent Dynamic Style rules in the Style tab, where styling now lives - and where it also reaches the globe, and can drive weight and opacity. The entries themselves are left alone; they still draw the legend.

components.name: Legend
components.description: Configures a legend for the layer. The Legend Tool renders symbologies and gradient scales for any properly configured layer that is on. A layer with a Dynamic Style also has that style's scale drawn, after these entries.

object.name: Fill Color
object.description: A color for the main fill of the symbol.

object.name: Border Color
object.description: A stroke/border color. Note that 'discreet' and 'continuous' shapes have no borders.

object.name: Label
object.description: A label description for this legend entry.

object.name: Shape
object.description: The symbol for which to use for this legend entry. Discreet and continuous describe scales. These scales are broken into groups by a change in shape value. For instance, 'discreet, discreet, discreet, circle, discreet, discreet' represents a discreet scales of three colors, a circle and then a discreet scale of two colors.

object.name: Shape From Icon
object.description: Shape but taken from the Material Design Icon (mdi) library. Takes priority over the value in the 'shape' field. See https://pictogrammers.com/library/mdi/

object.name: Shape From Image
object.description: A URL to a custom image (jpeg|jpg|gif|png|svg|webp) for which to use for this legend entry. If the path is relative, it will be relative to the mission's directory. This field will override values in the Shape and Shape From Icon fields.

object.name: Property Name
object.description: The name of the property to match for this legend entry.

object.name: Property Value
object.description: The value of the property to match for this legend entry.

object.name: Style Matching (deprecated)
object.description: Deprecated and no longer applied: legend entries describe the legend, they don't style features. Use Dynamic Style in the Style tab instead - the 'Convert to Dynamic Style' button above migrates these entries for you.

object.name: Hide From Legend
object.description: If true, this legend entry will be hidden from the legend.

rows.name: Interactions
rows.description: Choose a legacy Kind preset or compose an ordered click-interaction pipeline. Infrastructure interactions remain automatic.

components.name: Initial Filters
components.description: Configures the layer's filters for displaying an initial custom subset of the data.

object.name: Type of Property
object.description: If not a Group, whether the property's value should be treated as a string or as a number.

object.name: Property
object.description: If not a Group, a field name from the properties object of each feature of this layer to be to construct a filter. Supports dot.notation for nested properties.

object.name: Operator
object.description: If not a Group, the operator to use between the 'Property' and 'Value'.

object.name: Value
object.description: If not a Group, a value for the equation to operate on.

object.name: Is A Group
object.description: A group contains all property-value rows beneath this row and up until the next Group row or up until the end. Groups themselves are always ANDed together but enables member rows within them to abide by a different operator. If this entry 'Is A Group', then the type, property, operator and values fields are ignored.

object.name: Group Operator
object.description: If 'Is A Group', the operator to use for members within the group. 'AND' ands all the group members together. 'OR' ors all the group members together. 'NOT_AND' ands all the group members together and then negates the evaluation. 'NOT_OR' ors all the group members together and then negates the evaluation.

rows.name: Interface
rows.subdescription: The property key whose value should be the hover text of each feature. If left unset, the hover key and value will be the first one listed in the feature's properties.

components.name: Alt + {letter} Toggle Shortcut
components.description: A single letter to 'ALT + {letter}' toggle the layer on and off. Please verify that your chosen shortcut does not conflict with other system or browser-level keyboard shortcuts.

components.name: Search Construct
components.description: When set, this layer will become searchable through the search bar at the top. The search will look for and autocomplete on the properties specified. All properties are enclosed by parentheses and space-separated. 'round()' can be used like a function to round the property beforehand. 'rmunder()' works similarly but removes all underscores instead. For example: '(RMC) rmunder(sol)'

components.name: External Links
components.description: Configure deep links to other sites based on the properties on a selected feature. Upon clicking a feature, a list of deep links are put into the top bar and can be clicked on to navigate to any other page.

object.name: Display Name
object.description: The name of the deep link. It should be unique.

object.name: URL
object.description: A url template. Curly brackets are included. On feature click, all '{prop}' are replaced with the corresponding features[i].properties.prop value. Multiple '{prop}' are supported as an access to nested props using dot notation '{stores.food.candy}'.

components.name: TopBar Information
components.description: Creates an informational record at the top of the page. The first use case was showing the value of the latest sol. Clicking this record pans to the feature specified by 'which'. This is used on startup and not when a user selects a feature in this layer.

object.name: Information Construct
object.description: A name to display. All '{prop}'s will be replaced by their corresponding features[which].properties[prop] value.

object.name: Icon Name
object.description: Any Material Design Icon name: https://pictogrammers.com/library/mdi/

object.name: From Feature
object.description: This only supports the value 'last' at this point meaning that the properties from the last feature in the layer while be used to populate the information in the TopBar.

object.name: Go
object.description: if true, pans and zooms to the feature of which on initial load. The zoom used is Map Scale Zoom or the current zoom. In the case of multiple layers configured with 'Go', only the first feature with info.go is gone to.

rows.name: Information
rows.subdescription: Assign tags to this layer so that they may be searched upon through the LayersTool. A category may be specified with the following pattern: 'category:tag'
A freeform markdown description of the layer. In the LayersTool, users may click the information icon beside the layer's name to view this information.

components.name: Enabled
components.description: If true, tries to only query the vector features present in the user's current map viewport. This can be very performant for large vector datasets especially if minimum and maximum zooms are set for the layer. Pan and zooming causes requeries. If used with a geodataset, the time and extent queries will work out-of-the-box. Otherwise, if using an external server, the following parameters in {} will be automatically replaced on query in the url: 'starttime={starttime}&endtime={endtime}&startprop={startprop}&endprop={endprop}&crscode={crscode}&zoom={zoom}&minx={minx}&miny={miny}&maxx={maxx}&maxy={maxy}'. This setting is not advised if the data source is a straight geojson file because it expects a server that can crop the data to given extents.

components.name: Threshold
components.description: If dynamicExtent is true, only requery if the map was panned past the stated threshold. Unit is in meters. If a zoom-dependent threshold is desired, set this value to a string ending in '/z'. This will then internally use 'dynamicExtentMoveThreshold / Math.pow(2, zoom)' as the threshold value.

components.name: Don't Return Duplicates
components.description: If checked, only the first of a series of duplicated features from a GeoDataset is returned. If the GeoDataset uses a 'Group Id', it will be used to check whether features are duplicated. If a 'Group Id' is not set, the geometry field will be used to check for duplicated features. Using the geometry field may result in more of a performance hit for massive GeoDatasets. This functionality is useful, for instance, when many features with differing properties shared the same geometry.

components.name: Get Feature Properties on Click
components.description: Works just like Dataset links to get feature properties. For performance reasons, if checked, the main GeoDataset will be returned with only DB row ids or, if set, 'Group Id' and 'Feature Id' and will requery the rest of the feature's properties on-click. If a 'Group Id' is specified for the GeoDataset, all properties for every feature within its group will be returned as this makes it possible to still access every feature even while 'Don't Return Duplicates' is set.

components.name: Group Statistics Fields
components.description: Comma-separated numeric field names to summarize per 'Group Id' group. Each feature comes back with '_.stats.<field>' holding the group's 'min', 'max' and 'avg' - so a feature can be styled or labelled by its group rather than only by itself, e.g. by the property '_.stats.depth_m.avg'. Fields named by a Dynamic Style rule are requested automatically.

components.name: Property Key of Unique Id
components.description: In the case of deep-linking to certain features, a feature.properties key/field name is needed that points to a unique id in order to reselect it. dot.notation.is.supported for nested fields. You must make sure unique key values exist per feature for this to function properly. It is advised to set this if 'Dynamic Extent' is enabled.

components.name: Disable Interactivity
components.description: If checked, no mouse events will trigger on features of this layer.

components.name: Connections
components.description: Datasets are csvs uploaded from the 'Manage Datasets' page accessible on the lower left. Every time a feature from this layer is clicked with datasetLinks configured, it will request the data from the server and include it with it's regular geojson properties. This is especially useful when single features need a lot of metadata to perform a task as it loads it only as needed. A unique value needs to be present in both the feature's 'prop'erties and in the dataset's 'column' in order to combine the metadata.

object.name: Dataset Name
object.description: The name of a dataset to link to. A list of datasets can be found in the 'Manage Datasets' page.

object.name: Connecting Dataset Column
object.description: This is a column/csv header name within the dataset. If the value of the prop key matches the value in this column, the entire row will be return. All rows that match are returned.

object.name: Connecting Feature Property
object.description: This is a property key already within the features properties. It's value will be searched for in the specified dataset column.

object.name: Connecting Feature Display Name Property
object.description: This is a property key within the returned dataset feature properties. This is effectively an optional second-order property key. In the case of multiple dataset row entries being returned, this is useful for users of the UI to be able to distinguish between them. If unset, defaults to the value of 'Connecting Feature Property'.

components.name: Chemistry Values
components.description: Comma-separated chemistry columns to use as percentages and in what order. Should be used with a Dataset. Ex. 'Al2O3,CaO,FeOT,K2O,MgO,Na2O,SiO2,TiO2'. Look into the docs for the ChemistryTool for more information.

components.name: Hide Main Features
components.description: If true, hides all typically rendered features. This is useful if showing only the 'Attachments' of layers is desired and not their features themselves.
